div.div:
The only entry point that pulls pixels
render() pulls them later, while slicing; layoutPagesFromHeaders()
never pulls any. Here the whole point is the copy-out, so the cost
is a full decode and scale of one page.
The caller allocates and owns rgba — no allocation crosses the
library boundary. A size mismatch throws rather than writing a
plausible-looking wrong image, so a stale layout surfaces at once.

div.div:
Why the result is always RGBA8888
sRGB is 8-bit by definition in libvips, so the colourspace call
settles both space and depth; addalpha then fixes the band count.
Both are no-ops for a page that already is 8-bit sRGB RGBA.
The narrowing is for the caller's convenience — the committed
render still keeps the source's own format.
